planningPrinciples: Use one practical hotel base per city; the only intentional return is the final two Seoul nights for a low-stress ICN departure.
Travel by direct KTX on city-change days, with only a light neighborhood plan after check-in.
Group sights by neighborhood rather than crisscrossing each city for a single attraction.
Keep a weather-friendly indoor alternative every day and avoid making time-sensitive events the sole anchor.
Treat all rail times, event dates, pricing, opening hours, and entry rules as details to verify in official apps and sites before purchase.

importantDates.label: CSAT / Suneung day
importantDates.note: Keep this Busan day deliberately low-stakes. The retained emergency research flags morning traffic management, later office/bank opening, and an approximately 13:05–13:40 aviation hold; verify the current notice before travel.

importantDates.label: 13:00 ICN departure
importantDates.note: Plan to be at the airport around three hours before an international departure, subject to airline guidance. Stay in Seoul the final two nights instead of attempting a same-day Busan-to-ICN connection.

trip.sourceNote: These are deliberately detailed planning blueprints synthesized from the retained transport, hotel, activity, food, savings, and emergency research. They are not confirmations or a live timetable.

itineraries.title: Capital, science city, and coast
itineraries.bestFor: Travelers who want the broader third-city experience: science and design spaces, bakery culture, parks, hot springs, and more restaurant variety without giving up a clean KTX route.
itineraries.decisionSummary: This is the stronger choice when the middle stop should feel like a real city stay rather than only a rail-efficient pause. It adds a little more rail distance than Cheonan but gives five nights enough texture to justify the move.
itineraries.tradeoff: Daejeon is farther south than Cheonan, so city-change days need slightly more rail time. Keep the hotel near Daejeon Station or commit to a short taxi on KTX days rather than creating a luggage-heavy local transfer.

scorecard.label: Rail flow
scorecard.value: Direct KTX on all three long legs

scorecard.label: Value
scorecard.value: Strong station-area and mid-range hotel options

scorecard.label: Middle-city depth
scorecard.value: Science, parks, food, hot springs, design

scorecard.label: Hotel strategy
scorecard.value: One base near Daejeon Station / old downtown

bases.why: Easiest late arrival, straightforward airport access, and a familiar final-night base before ICN. Use the same neighborhood for both Seoul legs to reduce decision fatigue.
hotelIdeas: Nine Tree by Parnas Seoul Myeongdong 1

bases.why: This is the value-and-convenience base: easy KTX arrival and departure, Sojaedong and Sungsimdang nearby, plus simple taxi or subway access to Expo Park and Yuseong.
A single Haeundae base gives the coastal portion a higher-quality feel without another hotel move. Dedicate one full west-Busan day to Gamcheon, Jagalchi, and Nampo rather than relocating mid-stay.
hotelIdeas: Ramada Encore by Wyndham Busan Haeundae

transfers.recommended: Pre-plan the door-to-door option that matches the final hotel and immigration timing: airport limousine or official taxi is the calm default after a 21:00 arrival; use AREX only if the last service, hotel connection, and luggage handling still make sense.
transfers.why: A late first night is not the time to optimize a small fare difference. Confirm hotel late check-in and save its Korean address before departure.

transfers.recommended: Take a late-morning or early-afternoon direct KTX from Seoul Station. Use a taxi for the final station-to-hotel connection if luggage would make a local transfer annoying.
transfers.why: The day stays relaxed, leaves time for breakfast/check-out, and protects the first Daejeon evening.

transfers.recommended: Book a direct KTX around late morning. Go straight to the Haeundae hotel, drop bags, then make only a beach or neighborhood walk the anchor that night.
transfers.why: You arrive refreshed enough to enjoy Busan instead of turning the transfer into a sightseeing marathon.

transfers.recommended: Take a direct KTX back to Seoul in late morning or early afternoon, then use the evening for check-in, laundry, packing, and an easy familiar neighborhood meal.
transfers.why: The two-night Seoul buffer protects the 13:00 ICN departure from rail delays or a stressful same-day connection.

transfers.recommended: Leave the hotel early enough to arrive at ICN around three hours before departure, following airline advice. AREX Express is a good fit near Seoul Station; an airport limousine or taxi can be better for a hotel away from the rail hub or with heavy bags.
transfers.why: International check-in, baggage, tax-refund tasks, terminal uncertainty, and security make the final morning a logistics day, not a sightseeing day.

bookingPriorities: Book the first Seoul hotel with confirmed late check-in before choosing the arrival transfer.

Once dates are firm, set alerts for the Seoul→Daejeon, Daejeon→Busan, and Busan→Seoul KTX legs. Re-check Korail's actual release window, train number, luggage policy, and seat map rather than relying on a generic calendar rule.
Book one Haeundae hotel for all seven Busan nights unless there is a compelling special rate. A hotel split costs time and reduces beach-day flexibility.
Reserve any must-do timed ticket only after the city bases are booked. Keep one indoor alternative unreserved for rain, wind, or fatigue.
Save Korean hotel addresses, KTX confirmations, and final flight details to the local planner as soon as they exist.

days.title: Land softly; do not turn arrival into a sightseeing day
days.anchor: ICN arrival at 21:00 → hotel → sleep

blocks.label: Before landing
blocks.text: Keep passports, arrival confirmation, insurance details, and the hotel’s Korean address in one offline note. Confirm the hotel will accept a late arrival.

blocks.label: At ICN
blocks.text: Complete immigration and baggage collection without a hard timetable. Buy or activate connectivity, withdraw only a small emergency cash amount if needed, and save 112, 119, and 1330.

blocks.label: To the hotel
blocks.text: Use the pre-selected late-night transfer. Choose the airport limousine or an official taxi when it removes a confusing luggage transfer; only use AREX if the actual last train and final walk are comfortably workable.

blocks.label: Night
blocks.text: Check in, hydrate, set alarms, and sleep. A convenience-store snack near the hotel is enough; preserve energy for the first full day.

days.food: Keep food simple: airport, hotel, or convenience-store backup only.
days.watchouts: No restaurant reservation, palace ticket, or long neighborhood walk belongs on this night.
days.planB: If immigration is slow or trains are no longer suitable, use the official taxi queue or hotel-arranged transfer rather than improvising.

days.title: Recovery pace in central Seoul
days.anchor: Myeongdong → Deoksugung stone-wall area → easy first-night dinner

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Sleep in, have a slow hotel breakfast, obtain/load a T-money or chosen payment card, and pin the hotel in Naver Map and KakaoMap.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Walk the compact Myeongdong–City Hall–Deoksugung area. This is intentionally low-navigation and gives you a feel for subway exits, convenience stores, and local meal timing.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Choose a simple Myeongdong meal and return early. If an official listing still confirms a first-days-only exhibition you truly want, use it as an optional indoor swap, not a required sprint.

days.food: Choose one Myeongdong food bookmark from the master library; prioritize a short walk from the hotel over a cross-city restaurant chase.
days.watchouts: Jet lag and a late arrival make a light walking loop more valuable than a packed museum list.
days.planB: If energy is low or weather is poor, make this a hotel-neighborhood, laundry, and map-setup day without guilt.

days.title: Museum-and-river indoor spine
days.anchor: National Museum of Korea → Yongsan / Itaewon dinner corridor

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Use Tuesday for the National Museum of Korea rather than a palace-dependent day. Give the collection enough time to be enjoyable; do not try to complete every gallery.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Walk or ride through Yongsan, then choose either the War Memorial area or an easy Itaewon/Hannam café and design stop based on your energy.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Eat in Yongsan or return toward Myeongdong before late-night crowds. Save an exact restaurant with Naver Map once you have seen its current hours.

days.food: Use a Yongsan or Itaewon food bookmark; reserve only if it is a true must-do.
days.watchouts: The source notes that Gyeongbokgung is typically closed Tuesday; verify all current closures before finalizing.
days.planB: Swap the afternoon for a café, Korean spa, or hotel rest if the museum becomes a full day.

days.title: Historic Seoul in one walkable cluster
days.anchor: Gyeongbokgung → Bukchon / Samcheong → Insadong → Gwangjang Market

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Arrive at Gyeongbokgung for the official opening and check the day’s changing-of-the-guard timing. Start at the palace so the rest of the day flows downhill through nearby neighborhoods.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Walk Bukchon and Samcheong slowly, respecting residential streets. Continue to Insadong for tea, crafts, or a museum rather than backtracking across Seoul.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Use Gwangjang Market for a casual food-focused finish, then take one direct subway or taxi back to the hotel.

days.food: Market grazing is the experience; keep a nearby classic-Korean or tea-house bookmark as a seated backup.
days.watchouts: Palace hours, closures, and crowd controls are live details. Dress for outdoor walking and check air quality first.
days.planB: If rain is heavy, center the day on the palace museum/nearby galleries, Insadong tea houses, and a market meal.

days.title: Hongdae, Yeonnam, and a flexible evening
days.anchor: Hongik University area → Gyeongui Line Forest Park → Yeonnam cafés

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Take Line 2 or AREX to Hongik University after rush hour. Begin with a slow walk through the Gyeongui Line Forest Park rather than a fixed attraction queue.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Browse Hongdae and Yeonnam at a neighborhood pace. Choose one café, a small shop, a PC bang, or an indie-cultural stop — not all of them.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Have dinner nearby, then decide in real time whether the energy and crowd level support staying for music/nightlife or returning early.

days.food: Use the master food list to choose ramen, Korean comfort food, or a café in the exact sub-neighborhood where you finish.
days.watchouts: Weeknight is more relaxed than Friday or Saturday, but keep bags close in dense pedestrian zones.
days.planB: If weather is poor, use an indoor café, shopping arcade, or museum and keep the forest walk brief.

days.title: Modern Seoul without a citywide zigzag
days.anchor: Seongsu → Seoul Forest → optional Gangnam / COEX

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Start in Seongsu for design shops, pop-ups, and coffee. Keep the exact shopping list open because pop-ups change quickly.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Walk Seoul Forest if weather is pleasant, then continue to Gangnam/COEX only if you still want the contrast of a large modern commercial district.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Eat in the neighborhood where you end. Avoid a long return-and-go-out loop before a Saturday day trip.

days.food: Seongsu café or Gangnam/COEX food option; select from the library after checking current wait times.
days.watchouts: Do not overbook branded pop-ups or assume a social-media listing is still active.
days.planB: Skip COEX and extend Seongsu/Seoul Forest if the day feels complete; that is the more relaxed version.

days.title: Low-friction day trip or an unhurried Seoul day
days.anchor: Suwon Hwaseong day trip, with Seoul fallback

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: If weather is good, take a straightforward train to Suwon and focus on the Hwaseong Fortress area. This is the source-recommended weekend alternative to an overcrowded Nami Island plan.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Walk only the fortress sections that fit your pace, have a local lunch, and return to Seoul before dark rather than maximizing every wall segment.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Pack the KTX day bag and have an easy Seoul dinner near the hotel. Confirm the following day’s train, station entrance, and check-out plan.

days.food: Suwon lunch if on the day trip; otherwise use a Seoul saved idea close to the hotel.
days.watchouts: Saturday crowds and weather determine whether the day trip is worth it. Do not force it just because it is in the draft.
days.planB: Stay in Seoul for Changdeokgung/Secret Garden if tickets and weather work, or use a museum-and-neighborhood day.

days.title: KTX to Daejeon; make the first evening local
days.anchor: Seoul hotel → Seoul Station → Daejeon Station → Sojaedong / old downtown

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Check out slowly, leave only with a confirmed KTX platform and a luggage plan. Buy a station snack if the train timing overlaps lunch.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Take the direct KTX, use a simple taxi or walk to the station-area hotel, and keep check-in as the main task.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Stroll Sojaedong or Daejeon Skyroad, then make Sungsimdang or a nearby old-downtown meal the reward for a successful transfer.

days.food: Sungsimdang bakery and one nearby dinner are a high-value, low-routing introduction to Daejeon.
days.watchouts: Do not schedule Expo Park or Yuseong on the same day unless the train and hotel timing are unusually generous.
days.planB: If rain or fatigue wins, use the hotel area and a bakery stop only.

days.title: Expo corridor and science-city evening
days.anchor: Expo Science Park → Hanbit Tower → Daejeon Shinsegae / Art Space 193

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Start after the commute peak and ride to Expo Science Park. Use the river and Hanbit Tower area as a relaxed outdoor orientation, not a race between every attraction.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Choose one indoor companion: Art Space 193, a Shinsegae stop, or a science-oriented attraction based on weather and interest.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Stay in the Expo/Yuseong side for dinner, then return directly to the hotel. The goal is a coherent district day, not a cross-town restaurant detour.

days.food: Use a Yuseong or Expo-area food bookmark; reserve only after current availability is clear.
days.watchouts: Individual museum/observatory schedules can vary by day. Confirm before leaving the hotel.
days.planB: Make the day entirely indoor with Art Space 193, aquarium/science options, and a mall meal.

days.title: Science museum, arboretum, and a spacious afternoon
days.anchor: National Science Museum → Hanbat Arboretum → Museum of Art area

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Use the National Science Museum as the main indoor anchor. Arrive early enough to enjoy it without trying to turn it into an all-day obligation.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Walk Hanbat Arboretum if conditions are good; pair it with the nearby art museum area only if you want more indoor time.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Return toward the old downtown for a casual market or noodle dinner, keeping the evening intentionally unstructured.

days.food: Daejeon’s central market or a saved noodle / Korean-food option makes the city’s food identity part of the day.
days.watchouts: Check closing days and last admissions for all museum stops.
days.planB: If cold rain makes the arboretum unattractive, add a second indoor exhibit or a longer café stop instead.

days.title: Nature-and-hot-spring contrast
days.anchor: Gyeryongsan / Donghaksa if clear; Yuseong hot-spring district if not

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Check weather and air quality first. On a clear day, make a modest Gyeryongsan or Donghaksa outing the one nature-focused experience of the Daejeon stay.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Return before exhaustion sets in. If outdoors are not appealing, use Yuseong’s hot-spring district, a footbath, and café time as the planned alternative rather than a consolation prize.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Have a relaxed Yuseong or old-downtown dinner and avoid another long ride.

days.food: Choose nearby Korean comfort food or a market item; this is a flexible day, not a reservation day.
days.watchouts: Trail conditions, weather, and local bus timing decide the outdoor version. Wear layers.
days.planB: Yuseong footbath / spa-style relaxation plus a café and museum is the official plan B, not a failure.

days.title: Local culture, bakery time, and a buffer before Busan
days.anchor: Jungang Market → Daejeon Skyroad → final Sungsimdang / packing break

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Keep the final full Daejeon day close to the station/old-downtown base. Browse Jungang Market and choose a small cultural stop rather than committing to a long regional excursion.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Use a bakery/café pause to review the Busan hotel, KTX, and saved map pins. This is the right place for logistics because tomorrow is a transfer day.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Take a final Skyroad or Sojaedong walk, eat nearby, and pack a train-day bag separate from the main luggage.

days.food: Repeat a favorite Daejeon bakery or choose a saved market-area meal. Repetition is convenient, not a missed opportunity.
days.watchouts: Avoid booking a late, far-away activity before the Busan move.
days.planB: If weather is bad, make the whole day a food-market, mall, and packing-buffer day.

days.title: KTX south; let Haeundae be the first impression
days.anchor: Daejeon → Busan KTX → Haeundae hotel → beach walk

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Check out, take a direct KTX to Busan, and use the station snack strategy instead of forcing a pre-train restaurant stop.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: From Busan Station, use a simple taxi or direct transit to the Haeundae hotel. Check in, orient on Line 2, and save the hotel address in Korean.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Walk Haeundae Beach or Dongbaek shoreline at sunset, then have a nearby dinner. Stop early if the wind is strong or the train day feels long.

days.food: Haeundae dinner close to the hotel; save the Busan Station fish-cake stop for an easy snack if timing fits.
days.watchouts: Avoid trying to combine arrival with Gamcheon or a cable car. Western Busan deserves its own day.
days.planB: Use a Haeundae café, hotel rest, and indoor dinner if coastal weather is rough.

days.title: Coastal day with a bookable evening spectacle
days.anchor: Blue Line Park / Cheongsapo → Haeundae → Gwangalli evening

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Use the Haeundae–Cheongsapo coast while you are fresh. Pre-book any Blue Line Park or Sky Capsule element you care about; otherwise use the public coastal walk and keep the pace simple.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Return through Haeundae for a late lunch and unstructured beach/café time. Do not add a western-Busan attraction just to fill the middle of the day.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Have dinner around Gwangalli and, if the official schedule still confirms it, watch the Saturday drone light show. Treat the show as optional because weather can change the experience.

days.food: Haeundae for lunch, Gwangalli for dinner; use the food library’s neighborhood filter rather than crossing back for a single saved restaurant.
days.watchouts: Weekend queues and weather matter; make advance reservations only for the one paid coastal activity you truly value.
days.planB: Swap the outdoor portions for Spa Land Centum City, Shinsegae, and an indoor view/meal.

days.title: West Busan in one deliberate sweep
days.anchor: Gamcheon Culture Village → Jagalchi → BIFF / Gukje → Yongdusan

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Leave Haeundae early for Gamcheon. Go directly there while light is good and accept that it is the transit-heavy day of the Busan stay.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Continue downhill toward Jagalchi and the BIFF/Gukje market zone. This sequencing keeps the day geographically coherent and leaves no need to backtrack to Haeundae until evening.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Use Yongdusan/Busan Tower only if you still have energy, then return to Haeundae in one direct ride or taxi.

days.food: Jagalchi / Nampo seafood or market snack is the natural food anchor; use a specific saved place only if its hours work.
days.watchouts: This is the longest local-transit day. Use a taxi for one leg if weather, fatigue, or hills make the value worthwhile.
days.planB: If rain makes Gamcheon unpleasant, do Nampo/Jagalchi/Busan Tower first and use an indoor Busan museum or department store.

days.title: Temple and coast, paced for a Monday
days.anchor: Haedong Yonggungsa → Songjeong / Haeundae coast

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Use the outdoor Haedong Yonggungsa temple visit on a day when many museums may have limited or closed hours. Go early for calmer paths and better light.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Continue to Songjeong or back along the coastal corridor for a beach café, rail-park segment, or simply open time.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Return to Haeundae for a relaxed dinner. Protect this lighter day after the full western-Busan outing.

days.food: Coastal café/lunch and a simple Haeundae dinner are sufficient.
days.watchouts: Coastal wind can make temple stairs and viewpoints less pleasant; check weather before committing.
days.planB: Use Centum City, Spa Land, and indoor food halls when rain or high wind is forecast.

days.title: Centum, F1963, and an indoor-friendly Busan day
days.anchor: F1963 → Centum City → Spa Land or Busan X the Sky

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Start at F1963 or a nearby culture/design stop, then move toward Centum rather than bouncing between distant coastal neighborhoods.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Use Shinsegae Centum City for shopping, food, and a weather-proof reset. Add Spa Land if the group wants a deliberate Korean relaxation experience.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Choose one evening view or a good dinner, not both if the day has already been full.

days.food: Centum’s food options are convenient on an indoor day; use the savings and food research for any live visitor offer only after verifying terms.
days.watchouts: Spa rules, age policies, and closing hours must be checked live.
days.planB: Make the whole day an indoor spa/mall day if rain persists; it is designed for exactly that situation.

days.title: Choose one southern-coast adventure
days.anchor: Oryukdo Skywalk / Igidae coast OR Taejongdae / Yeongdo

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Choose only one direction: Oryukdo/Igidae for a coastal walk and views, or Taejongdae/Yeongdo for cliffs, harbor scenery, and a slower island-side outing.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Stay in the same geographic zone for lunch and one secondary stop. Resist adding another iconic area just because it looks close on a map.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Return to Haeundae before late evening, keeping tomorrow flexible for the CSAT-aware day.

days.food: Seafood or a Yeongdo snack is appropriate if you choose that route; otherwise pick a saved local option near the day’s finish.
days.watchouts: This is an outdoor/weather-first day. Wind, rain, and footwear should decide the option.
days.planB: Replace it with Busan Museum of Movies, aquarium, café streets, or a long spa visit.

days.title: CSAT-aware, indoor, and intentionally flexible
days.anchor: Slow morning → indoor Centum/BEXCO option → simple evening

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Avoid an early, time-critical move. Start later, give yourself extra transit buffer, and do not book an airport or intercity connection around the national testing disruption window.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Use an indoor, nearby choice such as Centum shopping/culture, a spa, or a café plan. If the official G-STAR listing still confirms a visit and you care about gaming, it can be an optional BEXCO anchor after checking ticket and crowd details.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Keep dinner close to the hotel and pack for tomorrow’s KTX return. Confirm the train, Seoul check-in, and airport-transfer preference.

days.food: Choose an easy nearby meal with a confirmed opening time; do not make a cross-city reservation the point of this day.
days.watchouts: The retained emergency source flags CSAT traffic management and a possible aviation hold; verify the current notice and avoid treating old timing as live fact.
days.planB: Hotel rest, shopping, room-service-style convenience food, and packing are all valid on this deliberately buffered day.

days.title: Return to Seoul; convert the evening into departure insurance
days.anchor: Busan KTX → Seoul hotel → easy neighborhood reset

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Check out without rushing, take the direct KTX back to Seoul, and avoid fitting in a final Busan attraction before the train.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Check in, run laundry if useful, organize souvenirs, and confirm airline terminal, online check-in, airport route, and terminal-specific timing.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Enjoy a close-by Seoul dinner and a short familiar walk. The success of this day is being settled, not maximizing a final attraction.

days.food: Return to a favorite Myeongdong/City Hall option or try one saved restaurant within a short walk of the hotel.
days.watchouts: Keep passports, tax-refund paperwork, and shopping receipts in one known place tonight.
days.planB: If the train arrives later than expected, skip everything except hotel check-in and a simple meal.

days.title: One final Seoul choice, then pack early
days.anchor: Choose one: favorite-neighborhood repeat, museum/design day, or final shopping

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Choose the one Seoul experience you would be disappointed to miss after the first leg: a palace/garden if weather and reservations work, a museum/design district, or a favorite neighborhood repeat.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Buy remaining gifts in a compact area, then return to the hotel before dinner. Keep receipts and tax-refund requirements organized as you shop.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Pack fully, weigh luggage if possible, set multiple alarms, and decide the exact hotel departure time for ICN. Have a final convenient dinner rather than a far-away farewell reservation.

days.food: Repeat your best Seoul meal or choose a final food-library favorite close to the hotel. Reliability beats novelty before departure.
days.watchouts: Saturday crowd density can make a long retail list frustrating. Make a short priority list and stop when it is done.
days.planB: Use a hotel-neighborhood day with a café, light shopping, and packing if the weather or energy does not support a full outing.

days.title: ICN departure at 13:00
days.anchor: Hotel → ICN → check-in / security / departure

blocks.label: Early morning
blocks.text: Check the airline app, passport, terminal, baggage, and any tax-refund process before leaving the room. Do not start new sightseeing or shopping.

blocks.label: Airport transfer
blocks.text: Leave early enough to be at ICN around three hours before the 13:00 international departure, following airline instructions. Choose AREX Express from Seoul Station when it is the simplest door-to-gate route; otherwise use limousine/taxi as appropriate.

blocks.label: At ICN
blocks.text: Complete check-in, baggage drop, any valid tax-refund steps, security, and gate transfer with time to spare. Eat after the essential steps are done.

days.food: Airport meal only after airline and security tasks are handled.
days.watchouts: Terminal, airline cutoff, tax-refund rules, and transit schedule must be reconfirmed close to departure.
days.planB: There is no sightseeing backup: the buffer itself is the plan.

itineraries.title: Capital, rail-smart heritage stop, and coast
itineraries.bestFor: Travelers who prioritize the quickest, most economical middle-city rail routing while still getting five relaxed nights of history, parks, local food, and a lower-cost hotel base.
itineraries.decisionSummary: This is the efficiency winner. Cheonan sits directly on the Seoul–Busan KTX corridor, shortening the middle rail leg and preserving more time for a calm hotel rhythm. Its experience list is narrower than Daejeon’s, but the itinerary makes that a feature: fewer decisions, less transit, and one excellent historical day.
itineraries.tradeoff: Cheonan’s top experiences are more concentrated and less varied than Daejeon’s. Choose it for the rail/hotel equation, not if you want five days of big-city science, museum, and nightlife variety.

scorecard.label: Rail flow
scorecard.value: Fastest, cleanest stop on the Seoul–Busan corridor

scorecard.label: Value
scorecard.value: Strong mid-range hotel pricing and short KTX legs

scorecard.label: Middle-city depth
scorecard.value: History, temple, market, relaxed local rhythm

scorecard.label: Hotel strategy
scorecard.value: Central Cheonan base + simple taxi to KTX hub

bases.why: Same arrival/departure logic as the Daejeon route: an easy late first night and a protected final ICN morning.
hotelIdeas: Nine Tree by Parnas Seoul Myeongdong 1

bases.why: A central base gives better evening food, markets, and local walkability. On KTX days, use a straightforward taxi to Cheonan-Asan rather than converting luggage movement into an extra local-train problem.
Stay in one good Haeundae base and make the west side a dedicated excursion; this creates a better beach/coast experience than a midweek hotel split.
hotelIdeas: Ramada Encore by Wyndham Busan Haeundae

transfers.recommended: Use the same late-arrival strategy as the Daejeon version: choose an airport limousine or official taxi if it removes stress; use AREX only when the actual late service and hotel connection are clean.
transfers.why: The trip begins with a 21:00 arrival, so convenience and confirmed late check-in outrank a small fare saving.

transfers.recommended: Take a late-morning or early-afternoon direct KTX toward Cheonan-Asan. Use a taxi to a central Cheonan hotel if that is your chosen base; do not drag bags through a local transfer simply because it looks cheaper on a map.
transfers.why: This is the route’s main value advantage: a compact, direct first rail leg while retaining a city-center hotel experience.

transfers.recommended: Taxi back to the KTX hub with time cushion, then take a direct KTX south. Go to the Haeundae hotel before doing only a light coastal evening.
transfers.why: Cheonan stays efficient when you plan the last-mile taxi as part of the route, not as a surprise.

transfers.recommended: Take the direct KTX back to Seoul and protect the final two nights for departure logistics, easy food, and a final flexible Seoul day.
transfers.why: A same-day Busan-to-ICN departure would make the 13:00 flight unnecessarily fragile.

transfers.recommended: Follow the exact terminal and airline timeline. Allow roughly three hours at ICN before a 13:00 international departure and choose AREX, limousine, or taxi based on the actual hotel location and bags.
transfers.why: The final Seoul base turns the airport run into one predictable transfer.

bookingPriorities: Pick a Seoul hotel that is explicitly comfortable with late check-in on Nov 1, then choose the airport transfer around it.
Set KTX alerts for Seoul→Cheonan-Asan, Cheonan-Asan→Busan, and Busan→Seoul. Confirm current Korail sale timing, actual departure station, seat availability, and luggage needs before paying.
For central Cheonan, pre-save a taxi route to Cheonan-Asan Station and build the fare/time into the rail day. For pure rail convenience, compare a Cheonan-Asan-area hotel instead.
Do not over-reserve Cheonan. The value of this route is a low-friction middle stop with room for local discoveries.
Keep any Busan coast train/capsule or major timed attraction to one intentional booking per day.

days.title: Land softly; do not turn arrival into a sightseeing day
days.anchor: ICN arrival at 21:00 → hotel → sleep

blocks.label: Before landing
blocks.text: Keep passports, arrival confirmation, insurance details, and the hotel’s Korean address in one offline note. Confirm the hotel will accept a late arrival.

blocks.label: At ICN
blocks.text: Complete immigration and baggage collection without a hard timetable. Activate connectivity, retain a small emergency cash option if wanted, and save 112, 119, and 1330.

blocks.label: To the hotel
blocks.text: Use the pre-selected late-night transfer. An airport limousine or official taxi is the calm default if it removes a confusing bag transfer; use AREX only when the live last-service and final walk are comfortably workable.

blocks.label: Night
blocks.text: Check in, hydrate, set alarms, and sleep. A simple snack is enough; the itinerary begins tomorrow.

days.food: Keep food simple: airport, hotel, or convenience-store backup only.
days.watchouts: No restaurant reservation, palace ticket, or long neighborhood walk belongs on this night.
days.planB: If immigration is slow or trains are no longer suitable, use the official taxi queue or hotel-arranged transfer rather than improvising.

days.title: Recovery pace in central Seoul
days.anchor: Myeongdong → Deoksugung stone-wall area → easy first-night dinner

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Sleep in, have a slow breakfast, obtain/load a T-money or chosen payment card, and pin the hotel in Naver Map and KakaoMap.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Walk the compact Myeongdong–City Hall–Deoksugung area. This is intentionally low-navigation and lets you learn transit, convenience stores, and meal timing.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Choose a simple local dinner and return early. An official first-days-only exhibition can be an optional indoor swap only if energy and live details support it.

days.food: Choose one Myeongdong food bookmark; a short walk from the hotel matters more than the perfect first meal.
days.watchouts: Jet lag makes a low-stakes neighborhood day the quality choice.
days.planB: Use the day for hotel rest, laundry, and map setup if energy is low.

days.title: Museum-and-river indoor spine
days.anchor: National Museum of Korea → Yongsan / Itaewon dinner corridor

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Use Tuesday for the National Museum of Korea rather than a palace-dependent day. Give the collection enough time to be enjoyable.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Walk or ride through Yongsan, then choose either the War Memorial area or an easy Itaewon/Hannam café and design stop based on energy.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Eat in Yongsan or return toward Myeongdong before late-night crowds.

days.food: Use a Yongsan or Itaewon saved food option after checking current hours.
days.watchouts: The retained research notes a typical Tuesday Gyeongbokgung closure; verify current palace schedules.
days.planB: Let the museum become a full day and skip the second neighborhood.

days.title: Historic Seoul in one walkable cluster
days.anchor: Gyeongbokgung → Bukchon / Samcheong → Insadong → Gwangjang Market

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Arrive at Gyeongbokgung for the official opening and confirm the current changing-of-the-guard schedule. Start at the palace so the route flows naturally through nearby districts.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Walk Bukchon and Samcheong with respect for residential streets, then continue to Insadong for tea, crafts, or one compact museum.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Use Gwangjang Market for a casual food-focused finish and return to the hotel in one direct ride.

days.food: Market grazing plus a nearby tea-house or classic-Korean backup.
days.watchouts: Palace hours, crowd controls, and air quality are live checks.
days.planB: Palace museums, Insadong tea houses, and market food make a coherent rain version.

days.title: Hongdae, Yeonnam, and a flexible evening
days.anchor: Hongik University area → Gyeongui Line Forest Park → Yeonnam cafés

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Travel to Hongik University after rush hour and start with the Gyeongui Line Forest Park.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Browse Hongdae and Yeonnam slowly. Choose one or two interests — café, small shops, PC bang, or music/culture — rather than completing a list.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Dine nearby, then decide in real time whether crowd and energy support staying for music/nightlife.

days.food: Choose a nearby food bookmark after you have checked the actual queue and closing time.
days.watchouts: Keep a modest walking radius and use the hotel as an easy reset if crowds feel tiring.
days.planB: Use indoor cafés and shops, then return early.

days.title: Modern Seoul without a citywide zigzag
days.anchor: Seongsu → Seoul Forest → optional Gangnam / COEX

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Start in Seongsu for design shops, pop-ups, and coffee. Check what is actually active before building the day around a temporary activation.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Walk Seoul Forest if weather is pleasant, then continue to Gangnam/COEX only if the group still wants the modern commercial contrast.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Eat where the day ends; do not create an extra cross-city trip before Saturday.

days.food: Seongsu café or Gangnam/COEX meal selected from the library after a live check.
days.watchouts: Temporary pop-ups are not reliable anchors.
days.planB: Extend Seongsu and skip COEX; it is the calmer version.

days.title: Low-friction day trip or an unhurried Seoul day
days.anchor: Suwon Hwaseong day trip, with Seoul fallback

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: If weather is good, take a straightforward train to Suwon and focus on the Hwaseong Fortress area. The retained transit research calls this a calmer weekend alternative to a crowded Nami Island plan.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Walk only the fortress sections that fit your pace, have lunch, and return to Seoul before dark.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Pack the KTX day bag, confirm the Cheonan transfer, and keep dinner close to the hotel.

days.food: Suwon lunch if you go; otherwise a nearby Seoul saved idea.
days.watchouts: Saturday weather/crowd conditions decide whether the trip is worth it.
days.planB: Stay in Seoul for a reserved garden, museum, or favorite neighborhood repeat.

days.title: Short KTX hop; set up Cheonan as an easy base
days.anchor: Seoul → Cheonan-Asan KTX → central Cheonan hotel → market / city-center walk

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Check out unhurriedly and take a late-morning or early-afternoon KTX. This is a short rail day, but keep a time cushion for the station and hotel handoff.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: From Cheonan-Asan, take the pre-saved taxi to the central hotel if that is your base. Check in, save the local address, and locate the closest food and convenience options.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Use Cheonan Central Market or the station-area streets for a light first evening. If a local sports/event listing is still live and timing is effortless, it can be a bonus — never the reason to rush the transfer.

days.food: Start with Hakwha walnut pastry if convenient, then choose a central Cheonan meal from the food library.
days.watchouts: Cheonan-Asan is the KTX hub; central Cheonan is the more lived-in base. Planning a taxi intentionally makes both work well.
days.planB: Check in, eat near the hotel, and leave all sightseeing for tomorrow.

days.title: Slow local orientation and market rhythm
days.anchor: Cheonan Station / city center → Arario area → local food

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Use Monday as a low-pressure orientation day: Cheonan Station, city-center streets, the Arario outdoor-sculpture/gallery area, and a café or shopping pause.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Browse the central market and Street of Culture at a local pace. This leaves the more closure-sensitive museum/Independence Hall combination for later in the week.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Have dinner near the hotel and identify the taxi pickup point you will use on KTX day.

days.food: Central Cheonan food bookmark, walnut pastry, and market snacks work naturally here.
days.watchouts: Monday can have attraction closures; a flexible city-and-food day avoids wasted transport.
days.planB: Use a hotel breakfast, department-store/café time, and a short local walk only.

days.title: The historical anchor day
days.anchor: Independence Hall of Korea → maple avenue / grounds → Byeongcheon food stop

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Make Independence Hall the one deliberately full excursion of the Cheonan stay. Confirm museum hours and use a taxi/bus plan that lets you arrive with energy.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: See the exhibition halls and grounds at a humane pace; use the maple avenue or outdoor route only if the weather is inviting.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Have a Byeongcheon-style local food stop if its current hours work, then return directly to the hotel rather than adding a second distant attraction.

days.food: Byeongcheon sundae is the natural regional experience; keep a central Cheonan backup if the excursion runs long.
days.watchouts: Exhibition schedules, buses, and weather should be checked the evening before.
days.planB: If weather or opening details are poor, use Cheonan museums/galleries and defer the hall to the clearest day.

days.title: Temple, park, and city-view day
days.anchor: Gakwonsa Temple → Cheonan Samgeori Park → city-center evening

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Visit Gakwonsa Temple and its giant bronze Buddha while conditions are calm. Give yourself enough time for the grounds instead of adding another temple on the same day.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Pair it with Samgeori Park or a relaxed Cheonan City Hall / skyline viewpoint if the weather is good. Keep the routing within the same side of the city.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Return to central Cheonan for dinner and a café, leaving the second half of the trip intentionally unhurried.

days.food: Use a central food bookmark after returning; do not make food a distant second excursion.
days.watchouts: Outdoor steps and parks are weather-sensitive; wear layers and choose a taxi if the local connection is inconvenient.
days.planB: Arario Gallery, an indoor café, and the market make an easy urban substitute.

days.title: A deliberately open value day
days.anchor: Choose one: postal/culture museum, relaxed café circuit, or a nearby Asan hot-spring-style break

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Choose the version of Cheonan you want more of: a compact museum/culture stop, a relaxed food-and-café loop, or an Asan-side rest day if transport and current details are simple.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Keep this as a buffer rather than a list. Use it for anything missed at Independence Hall or the temple day, or simply slow down before Busan.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Pack the KTX bag, confirm tomorrow’s taxi to Cheonan-Asan and the Busan hotel check-in, then enjoy one easy final Cheonan dinner.

days.food: Use the city food list to repeat a favorite or try one specialty; this is the best night to avoid an overplanned meal.
days.watchouts: The point of Cheonan is efficient breathing room. Do not turn this into a forced Seoul day trip.
days.planB: Hotel rest, shopping, and packing are a successful version of the day.

days.title: KTX south; let Haeundae be the first impression
days.anchor: Cheonan-Asan → Busan KTX → Haeundae hotel → beach walk

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Taxi to Cheonan-Asan with a cushion, take the direct KTX to Busan, and use station food only if it avoids a rushed meal.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Use a straightforward transfer to the Haeundae hotel, check in, and save the hotel address in Korean.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Walk Haeundae Beach or the Dongbaek shoreline at sunset, then have a nearby dinner. Keep it light after the transfer.

days.food: Haeundae dinner close to the hotel; a Busan Station fish-cake snack is an easy optional stop.
days.watchouts: Gamcheon, Nampo, and the cable car deserve their own day; do not add them to arrival day.
days.planB: Use a Haeundae café, hotel rest, and indoor dinner if weather is rough.

days.title: Coastal day with a bookable evening spectacle
days.anchor: Blue Line Park / Cheongsapo → Haeundae → Gwangalli evening

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Use the Haeundae–Cheongsapo coast while you are fresh. Reserve only the coastal train/capsule component that is truly important; the walk itself is excellent value.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Return through Haeundae for food and beach/café time. Keep the middle open rather than forcing a second distant attraction.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Dine around Gwangalli and, only if the official schedule still confirms it, watch the Saturday drone light show.

days.food: Haeundae lunch, Gwangalli dinner; use neighborhood filtering in the food library.
days.watchouts: Weekend queues and weather matter. Make only one paid coast booking the non-negotiable.
days.planB: Spa Land Centum City and Shinsegae make a high-quality indoor coastal substitute.

days.title: West Busan in one deliberate sweep
days.anchor: Gamcheon Culture Village → Jagalchi → BIFF / Gukje → Yongdusan

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Depart Haeundae early for Gamcheon while light is good. Accept that this is the one transit-heavier day in Busan.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Continue toward Jagalchi and BIFF/Gukje; keeping the route west-to-central avoids wasteful backtracking.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Add Yongdusan or Busan Tower only if energy remains, then return directly to the hotel.

days.food: Jagalchi/Nampo seafood or market food is the natural anchor.
days.watchouts: Use a taxi for one hill or long connection if the value of saved energy beats a local-transit puzzle.
days.planB: Nampo/Jagalchi/indoor museum first; skip Gamcheon in sustained rain.

days.title: Temple and coast, paced for a Monday
days.anchor: Haedong Yonggungsa → Songjeong / Haeundae coast

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Use the outdoor Haedong Yonggungsa temple visit on a day when indoor attractions may have narrower hours. Go early for a calmer coastal path.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Continue through Songjeong or back along the coast for café time, a short beach walk, or one easy rail-park section.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Return to Haeundae for an uncomplicated dinner and rest.

days.food: Coastal café/lunch and a simple Haeundae dinner.
days.watchouts: Wind and temple stairs decide whether the outdoor version is enjoyable.
days.planB: Centum City and Spa Land give an indoor answer without wasting the day.

days.title: Centum, F1963, and an indoor-friendly Busan day
days.anchor: F1963 → Centum City → Spa Land or view option

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Start at F1963 or one nearby culture/design stop, then move toward Centum as a single connected district day.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Use Shinsegae Centum City for shopping/food and add Spa Land if you want a deliberate relaxation experience.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Choose one evening view or one good dinner, leaving enough energy for the final outdoor day.

days.food: Centum food halls and nearby café options are useful on an indoor day.
days.watchouts: Verify spa requirements and closing hours live.
days.planB: Make the day fully indoor with a spa, mall, and food hall.

days.title: Choose one southern-coast adventure
days.anchor: Oryukdo Skywalk / Igidae coast OR Taejongdae / Yeongdo

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Select one direction: Oryukdo/Igidae for a coastal walk and views, or Taejongdae/Yeongdo for cliffs and harbor scenery.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Remain in that geographic zone for lunch and a second small stop; do not turn one coastal outing into a cross-city marathon.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Return to Haeundae before late evening, leaving tomorrow low-stakes for CSAT.

days.food: Seafood or Yeongdo snack if that is the route; otherwise choose nearby food after seeing the day’s pace.
days.watchouts: Wind, rain, footwear, and daylight decide the outdoor option.
days.planB: Aquarium, museum, café streets, or a long spa stop.

days.title: CSAT-aware, indoor, and intentionally flexible
days.anchor: Slow morning → indoor Centum/BEXCO option → simple evening

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Avoid an early time-critical move. Start later and give yourself extra transit buffer around the national testing-day disruption notices.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Use an indoor choice near Centum/BEXCO, a spa, or café time. If an official G-STAR listing still confirms it and you care about gaming, it can be optional — check ticket, crowd, and timing details live.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Pack for tomorrow’s KTX, confirm Seoul check-in, and eat near the hotel.

days.food: Choose a nearby meal with confirmed hours; no cross-city reservation today.
days.watchouts: The retained emergency source flags CSAT traffic management and a possible aviation hold. Re-check current notices before travel.
days.planB: Hotel rest, shopping, packing, and simple food are intentional buffer uses.

days.title: Return to Seoul; convert the evening into departure insurance
days.anchor: Busan KTX → Seoul hotel → easy neighborhood reset

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Check out without rushing and take the direct KTX to Seoul. Do not add a final Busan attraction before the train.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Check in, run laundry, organize souvenirs, and confirm the airline terminal, online check-in, and ICN route.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Enjoy a close-by dinner and a familiar walk. Being settled is the win.

days.food: A close Myeongdong/City Hall favorite is ideal.
days.watchouts: Keep passports, receipts, and tax-refund paperwork in one place tonight.
days.planB: If rail arrival is late, go straight to hotel check-in and dinner.

days.title: One final Seoul choice, then pack early
days.anchor: Choose one: favorite-neighborhood repeat, museum/design day, or final shopping

blocks.label: Morning
blocks.text: Pick the single Seoul experience that still matters after the first leg: a weather-appropriate palace/garden, museum/design area, or favorite neighborhood repeat.

blocks.label: Afternoon
blocks.text: Buy remaining gifts in one compact district and return to the hotel before dinner. Keep receipts organized as you shop.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.text: Pack completely, set alarms, decide the hotel departure time for ICN, and keep dinner close.

days.food: Repeat your best Seoul meal or use one nearby saved favorite.
days.watchouts: Saturday crowds can turn a huge shopping list into stress; keep only a short priority list.
days.planB: Hotel-neighborhood café, light shopping, and packing is a complete final day.

days.title: ICN departure at 13:00
days.anchor: Hotel → ICN → check-in / security / departure

blocks.label: Early morning
blocks.text: Check airline app, passports, terminal, baggage, and any tax-refund process before leaving the hotel. Do not start new sightseeing or shopping.

blocks.label: Airport transfer
blocks.text: Leave early enough to be at ICN around three hours before the 13:00 international departure, following airline instructions. Use the simplest option for the actual hotel and bags.

blocks.label: At ICN
blocks.text: Complete airline and security tasks first; eat and browse only after the gate process is settled.

days.food: Airport food only after essential departure tasks are complete.
days.watchouts: Terminal, airline cutoff, tax-refund requirements, and airport transport must be confirmed near departure.
days.planB: The time buffer is the plan; do not add an activity.
